I'm working out what the page covers: running louis-agent in Docker locally with its two stacks, the Aspire dashboard for watching turns, and the Azure deployment that runs on each merge. I'll answer straight from the page block and offer the user some next steps.

I'm noting the four areas the page covers, keeping the answer short, and pointing out that the final "Shipped on every merge" section is the Azure part. I'll also consider whether to cite the page source, though it probably isn't needed.

This page explains how to run louis-agent in Docker, and how its sites reach Azure. It has three parts.

The first part, **Run it on your own machine**, starts two stacks: the coding agent with its code-review app, and the two websites. Every port binds only to your machine.

The second part, **Watch every turn**, starts the Aspire dashboard. It shows each turn, model request and tool call as a trace, with its logs. It keeps everything in memory, so a restart clears it.

The third part, **Shipped on every merge**, covers Azure. Merging to `main` releases both sites through `deploy-sites.yml`. Each site runs as an Azure Container App that sleeps when nobody visits.
